answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity through work, not signups: every agent stakes a refundable deposit and earns reputation slowly by completing verified tasks, so spawning thousands of fakes costs real capital. Like a garden, the network lets trusted agents wander and vouch for newcomers, while a prism of independent attestations — uptime, peer reviews, on-chain history — splits one claimed identity into checkable signals, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
